items.excerpt: OpenAI is testing editorial-style labels on ChatGPT product results — "best all-rounder," "best for beginners," "best cushioning" — a new ranking layer brands cannot buy but will be judged by.
items.rationale: A live test in ChatGPT shopping creates an unbuyable editorial ranking layer brands must now optimise for — concrete, dated, and directly actionable for GEO/AEO work.

items.excerpt: S4 Capital's Monks has started letting AI agents run autonomously for days at a stretch with no human supervising them, pushing agency production work from assisted to unattended.
items.rationale: A named agency group has crossed from assisted to unattended agent production — a specific operating change in how ad work gets made, not 'AI is reshaping agencies' commentary.

items.excerpt: Google released Nano Banana 2.1, its latest image generation and editing model, and it is already live inside AI Mode in Google Search — putting generative imagery directly in the search surface brands optimize for.
items.rationale: A shipped, versioned model now live inside AI Mode — generative imagery lands in the exact search surface brands compete in, changing what visual assets have to compete against.

items.excerpt: Pinterest's new AI-powered Beauty Guides translate hair and nail Pins into salon terminology with estimated costs, appointment times and maintenance needs — turning inspiration pins into a purchase path.
items.rationale: A shipped platform feature that converts inspiration browsing into a priced, bookable purchase path — a new AI-built funnel step beauty and retail brands can plan for.

items.excerpt: Google's John Mueller says his own server logs show AI training crawlers fetching sitemaps and RSS feeds, and recommends default sitemap names or RSS as the practical way to be found by them.
items.rationale: A named practitioner's log-based finding with a specific method — use default sitemap names or RSS so AI crawlers can discover your content — changes a site owner's checklist tomorrow.

dedup.note: First published day for the marketing section — news_data.json has no sections.marketing, so there is no in-section history and no history_digest; every pick is verdict 'new' with nearest ''. Per the orchestrator's instruction I did NOT dedup against other sections. Within-pool content dedup: 14 candidates, 5 kept, 9 dropped. Dropped as weak on the 'AI makes the story happen' test: Modern Retail Gen Alpha panel (shopper-attitude panel, AI incidental), Retail Dive store associates (service-script commentary, no shipped thing). Dropped as vendor thought-leadership with no verifiable capability/date/number: AdExchanger 'AI-built MMM, start with a thesis' (M Squared exec interview). Dropped as commentary/analysis without a concrete release or ruling: Adweek 'AI agents getting their hands on ad dollars' (industry 'grappling'), SEJ 'Google is fighting SERP tracking, AI agents may make it worse' (speculative). Dropped on the per-outlet cap of 2: Search Engine Roundtable 'Search Console generative-AI control page expanded' (third SER item and the weakest — a doc clarification). Dropped as marketing-adjacent AI-industry news: TechCrunch 'Musubi PolicyLM-1.7B content moderation model' (brand-safety link is indirect) and TechCrunch 'getting websites to let AI agents in' (third TechCrunch item, overlaps the crawler-access theme already covered by the Mueller pick), The Verge 'Wikimedia blames OpenAI rogue bots for May outage' (publisher infrastructure, same crawler cluster). No two candidates covered the same event, so no same-story collapse was needed; the three crawler/agent-access items (SEJ SERP tracking, TechCrunch agent access, Verge Wikimedia) are distinct events but one theme, and I kept only the Mueller item from that theme. Outlet spread in the final 5: Search Engine Roundtable 2, Digiday 1, TechCrunch 1, Search Engine Journal 1 — 4 distinct outlets, cap respected, no duplicate URLs. All 5 share the single marketing category, so each got a distinct accent from sources.json palette.
